clue.text: Game crossing

definitions.meaning: a card game for four players in two partnerships
a structure carrying a road or railway over a river or gap

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the partnership card game and the span built over a river.

clue.text: Lofty ambitions showing prejudice about a modern French writer

indicators.note: the word for prejudice is placed around the writer's name, like a fence about it

parts.note: prejudice is bias
André Gide, the twentieth-century French novelist and Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: Someone's grand aims betray a bias concerning a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand schemes or ambitious concepts are colloquially called big ideas, matching lofty ambitions.

clue.text: Exerting no driving force, learn unit construction

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are built up again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A motorist idles while learning how a unit is built.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with the gears disengaged transmits no power to the wheels, so it exerts no driving force.

clue.text: A collector of unconsidered trifles

parts.note: describes someone who picks up the leftover ears of grain after harvest, or scraps of information others overlook

explanation.definitionFit: One who gathers leftovers after reaping, and figuratively anyone collecting odds and ends of fact.

clue.text: Curse all articles, with a thousand and one repeated

parts.note: the English articles an, a and the, all three in turn
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
one is A, the indefinite article used again

explanation.surface: A grammarian swears at every article in a long sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' signals that A, already among the articles, is used a second time at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, and more loosely any execration.

clue.text: Illumination from Scottish clues?

parts.note: crossword answers are called lights, and Scotland is in the north, so lights from Scotland become the polar glow in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The aurora seen in high northern latitudes is commonly called this, a natural illumination of the night sky.

clue.text: Satellite fairy

definitions.meaning: a moon of Uranus, the largest of them
the queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Shakespeare's fairy queen and to the Uranian moon named after her.

clue.text: Time to muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The moment has come to think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: One insect, note, related on the father's side

parts.note: one is A
a gnat is a small flying insect
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A genealogist records an insect and a musical note among paternal kin.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a relative descended through the male line, so the word means kin on the paternal side.

clue.text: Weapon for a wearisome Lilliputian?

parts.note: a tiny tedious person is a small bore, and a gun of narrow calibre goes by that description too

explanation.walkthrough: Lilliputians are the tiny people of Gulliver's Travels; a bore is a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm with a narrow barrel calibre, such as a .22, is a weapon of this name.

clue.text: The low-down that is for a spirit

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the inside story
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Inside information is given about a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinn of Arabian folklore, a supernatural being, is a kind of spirit.

clue.text: One humorist, so note two

parts.note: to mark something is to note it
twain is an archaic word for two

explanation.surface: A comedian makes a remark in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American writer famed for wit, a celebrated humorist.

clue.text: Take preliminary steps to phone about a vessel, daily

indicators.note: the phoning word goes around the vessel word, enclosing it

parts.note: before a call you dial the number
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to ring about a ship every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means occurring every day or in the daytime, a formal synonym for daily.

clue.text: Prepared press statement for a charity appeal?

definitions.meaning: a printed release given to journalists
a gift of money or food given to those in need

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a document given out to the press and alms given to the poor.

clue.text: 5 classically

parts.note: the answer to 5 down given its Latin, scientific name

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin term is the scientific name for the northern dawn-like glow, as used by Galileo.

clue.text: Do certain changes if you like, it doesn't matter to me

indicators.note: the letters of the two words undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off proposed alterations to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is an everyday expression of indifference, equivalent to saying something is no concern of mine.

clue.text: In addition to an incomplete physical comparison

definitions.meaning: a comparison of health, as healthy as someone, with the person compared left out

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means besides, and also opens a comparison of health left unfinished.

clue.text: Mean members of the family?

parts.note: close can mean stingy, so tight-fisted relatives, though the phrase actually means immediate kin

explanation.definitionFit: Immediate family such as parents, siblings and children are the nearest kin.

clue.text: "The Betrayal"-a show for which no seats are left

definitions.meaning: an act of treachery, abandoning principles

definitions.text: show for which no seats are left
definitions.meaning: a performance where every ticket has been sold

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an act of treachery and an event for which all tickets are gone.

clue.text: A scold is even neater

definitions.meaning: trim is old slang for rebuke, so one who rebukes

explanation.definitionFit: It is the comparative of trim, tidier, and in old usage someone who gives a dressing-down.

clue.text: A cub as framed: you may count on this

indicators.note: framed in the sense of fabricated, so the letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A young scout is set up, and is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' also hints at the frame of beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame with sliding beads is a device used for counting and arithmetic.

clue.text: He has a taking way with him

definitions.text: He has a taking way with him

parts.words: He has a taking way with him
parts.note: a taking way normally means charm, but here it is a habit of taking other people's property

explanation.definitionFit: A house-breaker steals goods, so his way of life is literally taking things.

clue.text: Shakespearian character making not "Much Ado" but more about nothing

indicators.note: about signals that the word more is turned around into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A play title is altered from Much Ado About Nothing to something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the comedy title Much Ado About Nothing; the words 'not Much Ado but' are surface dressing, joining the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Montague lover of Juliet is one of Shakespeare's best-known characters.

clue.text: First and last, right leg is broken: cartilage required

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed into a new order
only the opening and closing letters of right are taken

explanation.surface: Someone has broken their right leg and needs cartilage repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and last' takes R and T from 'right'; with LEGIS, 'broken' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Advice to someone on thin ice: "Stop bluffing"

definitions.text: Advice to someone on thin ice
definitions.meaning: literally, get off the dangerous surface
a colloquial retort meaning stop pretending

explanation.definitionFit: It is a colloquial challenge to someone exaggerating, and literally an instruction to get off something.

clue.text: An Australian acacia is everything I have

parts.note: what I have is mine, my
everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone declares a wattle tree to be their whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: A myall is a species of Australian wattle tree with hard scented wood.

clue.text: Physically-handicapped fielding position

definitions.meaning: jokingly, having a leg that is too short
a close catching position on the leg side in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: SHORT LEG is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cricket fielding spot near the batsman, and literally a limb of reduced length.

clue.text: Vegetables on the golf course

definitions.meaning: leafy green vegetables such as cabbage
the closely mown putting areas around each hole

explanation.definitionFit: The word means leafy vegetables and also the putting surfaces found on a golf course.
